Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central and the Provincial Mercantile Registry (Commercial Register) for the province where the registered office is located

Governing statute

Spanish Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), primary incorporation rules in Articles 1-31 and 57-62; Commercial Registry Regulations approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996; Notarial Law rules applicable to company deeds

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública constitutiva) and subsequent filing with the Mercantile Registry

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 38 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

The SL must maintain a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid-up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution in a blocked incorporation account opened in the company's name before the deed is granted; the deposit is released only after commercial registration.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate issued by a competent technician or authorized body, fire-protection inspection, civil-defense evacuation plan, structural load and stability certificate for machinery floors, electrical installation certificate, municipal first-occupation verification, and occupational health and safety prevention plan under Law 31/1995 before commencement of production.

Paid-in capital rule: The SL must maintain a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid-up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution in a blocked incorporation account opened in the company's name before the deed is granted; the deposit is released only after commercial registration.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
At a formal meeting of the founding members of the Spanish limited company, it is unanimously resolved: (1) to approve the incorporation in the form of Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada under the name and bylaws annexed; each founder subscribes and fully pays the quotas allocated to them, evidenced by the bank deposit certificate presented to the meeting; (2) to adopt as the registered and tax office the premises located at [full address], province of [Province], Spain; (3) to appoint [Name] as sole administrator, [Name] as alternate administrator, and [Name] as secretary, conferring the necessary corporate and registry powers; and (4) to execute the public deed before the appointed notary, request provisional tax identification, and complete registration.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Consejería de Industria of the corresponding Autonomous Community and the municipal licensing authority, together with the national industrial registry under Law 21/1992 on Industry

Category: Municipal operating and opening license (licencia de apertura y funcionamiento), together with the industrial establishment communication or environmental activity authorization required for the production plant

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) at incorporation before a notary, with the final definitive NIF issued by the AEAT after registration in the Mercantile Registry. The NIF serves as both the corporate tax identification and the Spanish VAT identification (NIF-IVA). A non-resident shareholder or foreign entity must appoint a tax representative resident in Spain and file Form 036/037 with the AEAT to obtain a non-resident NIF or to register as a non-established taxable person for VAT purposes; registration must occur before commencing any taxable supply in Spain.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident SL is taxed under the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law (Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income; branches of foreign entities are taxed on Spanish-source income only; no pass-through treatment is available for SLs. — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) at incorporation before a notary, with the final definitive NIF issued by the AEAT after registration in the Mercantile Registry. The NIF serves as both the corporate tax identification and the Spanish VAT identification (NIF-IVA). A non-resident shareholder or foreign entity must appoint a tax representative resident in Spain and file Form 036/037 with the AEAT to obtain a non-resident NIF or to register as a non-established taxable person for VAT purposes; registration must occur before commencing any taxable supply in Spain.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation; resident SL is taxed under the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law (Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income; branches of foreign entities are taxed on Spanish-source income only; no pass-through treatment is available for SLs.

Available election forms

No check-the-box system. Statutory elections available under the Corporate Income Tax Law include the consolidated tax group regime (art. 64), the SOCIMI (REIT) special regime, patent box benefit, R&D and innovation tax credits, and the reduced corporate income tax rate for newly created businesses. Hybrid mismatch and anti-abuse rules under ATAD are mandatory and not elective; all elections must be filed via Form 036 or the annual corporate income tax return within the prescribed deadlines.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 85,000 for supply of goods and EUR 60,000 for supply of services under the simplified SME regime; non-established foreign entities have no economic threshold and must register with AEAT for VAT before making their first taxable supply in Spain.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of physical goods from Spain to territories outside the European Union qualify for a 0% IVA rate under Article 21 of Ley 37/1992, provided the exporter is the seller or the goods are shipped directly by or on behalf of the supplier and the goods leave the EU within 30 days of delivery. The export must be evidenced by customs documents showing the goods have physically departed the EU. Certain international services, including transport and ancillary services, processing of goods, and cross-border services to non-established businesses, may also be zero-rated where the place of supply is outside Spain or the services are directly linked to exported goods, subject to the general EU B2B place-of-supply rules.

  • Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo – DUA/SAD with customs acceptance and exit confirmation)
  • Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR Transport Document evidencing physical departure from the EU
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/payment receipt evidencing receipt of foreign currency proceeds
  • Commercial invoice, packing list, and proof of contract or purchase order supporting the export transaction

Spain does not maintain a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime for all taxpayers. However, the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) requires taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04 to submit VAT invoice and transaction records to AEAT electronically in near real time via webservice/API. Under the Verifactu and Crea y Crece regulations, B2B electronic invoicing is mandatory, and billing software must generate certifiable and tamper-evident invoice records; no AEAT pre-approval of each invoice is required.

The AEAT may retroactively increase or deny the 0% rate if the exporter fails to produce legally sufficient export evidence. Non-compliance triggers the VAT charge at the standard 21% rate plus statutory interest, and improper refund claims are subject to penalties under articles 191 and 194 of the Ley General Tributaria, ranging from 15% to 150% of the tax amount, depending on intent. Falsifying customs or VAT documents may give rise to criminal charges under article 305 of the Spanish Penal Code when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000. Fiscal clawbacks are generally limited to the four-year prescription period, but limitation is suspended in cases of fraud or failure to file returns.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain maintains full current and capital account convertibility by force of Article 63 TFEU and EU Directive 88/361/EEC. No exchange authorization is required for EUR, USD, CNY or any convertible currency flows for a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL). Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted but require: (1) formal dividend resolution recorded in the Junta General notarial deed; (2) distributable-reserve certification prepared under Spanish GAAP; (3) Impuesto sobre Sociedades settlement evidencing post-tax distributable earnings; and (4) statistical Balance of Payments declaration (Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior, S-1 form) to Banco de España for any transaction equal to or above EUR 50,000. Non-resident dividend withholding is 19% default, reduced to 0% for EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive qualified parents, or treaty-reduced (US 0%-5%; China 10%; Mexico 10%; Brazil 15%). No capital controls, minimum holding period, or prior authorization apply to inbound foreign capital into an SL.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No statutory surrender, repatriation deadline, or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in Spain. Export receipts for trading-card print/distribution sales may remain in foreign currency indefinitely. Obligations are limited to: (a) Balance of Payments statistical declaration to Banco de España for receipts equal to or above EUR 50,000 (S-1 portal submission); and (b) customs export documentation (Documento Único Administrativo - DUA) evidencing physical goods movement. Invoice currency is freely negotiable.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), in coordination with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) of the Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa, and SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias) for AML/CFT supervision.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Stripe Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Medium-High for operational clearing; Low for capital escrow purposes. Spain-licensed EMIs (authorized by Banco de España under Law 21/2011 implementing PSD2) and EU-passported EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, MangoPay, Currencycloud) may lawfully hold an SL's treasury and route SEPA/SWIFT payments. Legal constraints: (a) capital-injection escrow accounts are discouraged because EMIs do not file Banco de España S-1 balance-of-payments declarations and may reject the 'capital contribution' purpose code; (b) non-EU EMIs cannot passport into Spain and must contract as agent of an authorized EMI; (c) card-print supplier settlements in USD/CNY require the EMI to maintain SWIFT correspondent access. Recommended structure: EMI as settlement-only node (Stripe/MangoPay for card sales; Wise for USD supplier clearing) with the Santander/BBVA account as the anchor treasury account performing all BOP reporting.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident UBO with no prior Spanish financial footprint and contributions sourced from an overseas parent entity.

Root cause: Non-resident UBO with no prior Spanish financial footprint and contributions sourced from an overseas parent entity.

Defense evidence: (1) Notarized and apostilled deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución); (2) registral certificate of the foreign parent; (3) UBO declaration identifying all natural persons >25%; (4) three-month bank statements from the home-country relationship bank; (5) Spanish NIE/TIE of managing director; (6) certified Spanish translations (traductor jurado); (7) signed business plan with 24-month cash-flow projection; (8) lease or warehousing agreement proving Spanish business nexus; (9) source-of-wealth letter for the capital injection.
High-volume, low-ticket digital card sales generating 200-5,000 small credit-card transactions monthly (platform collection typology).

Root cause: High-volume, low-ticket digital card sales generating 200-5,000 small credit-card transactions monthly (platform collection typology).

Defense evidence: (1) Executed distribution agreements with licensed IP owners (Panini, Topps, or documented sub-license chain to issuer); (2) Stripe/Authorize.Net merchant statements showing settlement history; (3) holographic cold-foil production contracts and supplier purchase orders; (4) intellectual-property indemnity insurance certificate; (5) e-commerce site order flow and platform architecture description.
Supply-chain payments to counterparties in China/Hong Kong or Latin America flagged as higher-risk corridors (FATF grey-list or enhanced-jurisdiction typologies).

Root cause: Supply-chain payments to counterparties in China/Hong Kong or Latin America flagged as higher-risk corridors (FATF grey-list or enhanced-jurisdiction typologies).

Defense evidence: (1) Full supply-chain diagram manufacturer to warehousing to EU distribution; (2) commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and customs DUAs for at least three historical shipments; (3) ISO 9001 or equivalent manufacturer certificates; (4) bank reference letter from the supplier's bank (SWIFT); (5) supplier UBO certificate (when available); (6) written representation of no relationship with shell/front companies.
Capital contribution or shareholder loan disproportionate to declared revenue or company activity scale.

Root cause: Capital contribution or shareholder loan disproportionate to declared revenue or company activity scale.

Defense evidence: (1) Certified capital increase deed (escritura de ampliación de capital) or shareholder loan agreement (contrato de préstamo entre socios); (2) source-of-wealth declaration (declaración de patrimonio) from the contributing shareholder; (3) audited financial statements or modelo 200 tax return of the parent; (4) AEAT tax clearance certificate (certificado de estar al corriente); (5) board resolution authorizing the treasury transaction.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant routing: (1) SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent to the SL's EUR IBAN via TARGET2 (T2) using corporate purpose code CAPL or 'Capital contribution' in field 70; (2) intra-EU injection may use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant (SCT Inst, up to EUR 100,000 per instruction); (3) treat as Inversión Extranjera Directa (IED) and file the Post-Investment Declaration (Declaración Posterior de Inversión Extranjera) with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within one month of settlement; (4) simultaneous electronic S-1 submission to Banco de España via the DEC portal when transaction value equals or exceeds EUR 50,000; (5) supporting pack: notarized board resolution, share-issue certificate (certificado de titularidad), bank credit advice, and registry filing receipt.Primary rails for physical trading-card supply: (1) SWIFT MT103 for high-value supplier payments to China (USD/CNY via CHIPS/CIPS correspondents) and SCT for EU printers; (2) confirmed irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit (UCP 600) when initial supplier onboarding or payment terms exceed 30 days and the order is above EUR 50,000; (3) Commercial LC with 'bill of lading' and 'inspection certificate' as required documents; (4) payment terms of 30% TT advance plus 70% against B/L copy via MT103 for established suppliers; (5) for EU cross-border settlement, TARGET2-SEPA direct IBAN transfer; (6) settlement instruction must carry full invoice number, DUA customs reference, and ISO 20022 purpose code GDDS for goods imports; (7) for repatriation of US platform proceeds (Stripe), use USD accumulation in an EU EMI or direct SWIFT MT103 to the SL's EUR account with purpose code 'proceeds of goods sold'.Outright EUR/USD forward contracts (contratos a plazo) executed OTC under ISDA 2002 or the Spanish Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras (CMOF); no exchange license required when hedging documented commercial exposure.Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on CNY, MXN, and BRL for settling trade-invoice exposure where the underlying currency is non-convertible offshore; permitted when documented as hedge for forecasted card-printing imports or LatAm distribution receipts.Cross-currency swaps (permutas de divisas / FX swaps) converting USD sales proceeds into EUR working capital while avoiding active spot-market round-tripping.Plain-vanilla purchased FX call/put options (MiFID II non-complex status) to cap procurement currency upside; requires professional-client opt-up, documented hedge ratio under EMIR clearing thresholds, and execution under an investment-services agreement (Contrato de Servicios de Inversión) where NDFs are involved.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for operational clearing; Low for capital escrow purposes. Spain-licensed EMIs (authorized by Banco de España under Law 21/2011 implementing PSD2) and EU-passported EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, MangoPay, Currencycloud) may lawfully hold an SL's treasury and route SEPA/SWIFT payments. Legal constraints: (a) capital-injection escrow accounts are discouraged because EMIs do not file Banco de España S-1 balance-of-payments declarations and may reject the 'capital contribution' purpose code; (b) non-EU EMIs cannot passport into Spain and must contract as agent of an authorized EMI; (c) card-print supplier settlements in USD/CNY require the EMI to maintain SWIFT correspondent access. Recommended structure: EMI as settlement-only node (Stripe/MangoPay for card sales; Wise for USD supplier clearing) with the Santander/BBVA account as the anchor treasury account performing all BOP reporting.
